cards.a: StackWise links stackable Catalyst switches such as a 3750/3850 into one logical switch with an active/standby/member model, while VSS virtualizes two 6500/4500 chassis into one logical switch using a VSL and active/standby roles.

cards.q: What benefits do stacking and VSS provide?
cards.a: They provide a single control plane and management domain, shared configuration, higher port density, supervisor failover, and allow EtherChannels to span members so STP does not block redundant links.

cards.q: What is the physical link used by StackWise?
cards.a: StackWise uses the proprietary StackWise stacking cable to connect stackable switches into a single logical switch.

cards.q: What is the VSL in a VSS?
cards.a: The VSL (Virtual Switch Link) is the high-bandwidth link, usually 40G or 10G, that connects the two chassis in a VSS to synchronize state and exchange control traffic.

cards.q: What are the roles in a StackWise stack?
cards.a: The stack elects one active (master) switch that holds the control plane, one standby that takes over on failure, and the remaining switches are stack members.

cards.q: Why does a VSS need dual-active detection?
cards.a: If the VSL fails, both chassis could think they are the active virtual switch (split-brain); dual-active detection using VSSP/PAgP or BFD makes one side shut down switching to prevent a loop.

cards.q: What is a Multichassis EtherChannel (MEC) in VSS?
cards.a: MEC is an EtherChannel whose members span both chassis of the VSS, providing redundancy and full utilization because both halves are one logical switch.

cards.q: Which commands verify a StackWise stack versus a VSS?
cards.a: StackWise uses show switch, show switch stack-ports, and show switch neighbors, while VSS uses show vss, show switch virtual role, and show etherchannel summary.

cards.q: A stack of switches split into two; what is the likely cause?
cards.a: A stack split is usually caused by a faulty or removed StackWise stacking cable or missing switch provisioning, detected with show switch stack-ports.

cards.q: What is the key exam distinction between StackWise and VSS?
cards.a: StackWise connects stackable switches (such as 3750/3850) with a StackWise cable in an active/standby/member model, while VSS fuses two 6500/4500 chassis over a VSL into active/standby virtual switches with dual-active detection.

cards.q: What is the StackWise/VSS quick-review summary?
cards.a: StackWise and VSS both create one logical switch, StackWise linking stackables over a StackWise cable into active/standby/member, and VSS fusing two chassis over a VSL with dual-active detection, both allowing EtherChannels across members.
